title: Post-Shooting Statement Conflict Audit
scope: Scope: publicly retrievable, case-relevant factual statements by named TPUSA figures/associates after Sept. 10, 2025, through Aug. 15, 2026. Tributes and unrelated political commentary are not exhaustively transcribed.
provenance: Imported from charlie_kirk_tpusa_statement_conflict_audit_2025-2026.xlsx (supplied analysis workbook, Aug 15 2026). Conflict classifications, severity and confidence ratings are as supplied; this app renders them and cross-checks them against its own datasets.

statements.role: TPUSA spokesman; Charlie Kirk Show executive producer
statements.claim: Said authorities were telling the team that the killer/suspect had been brought into custody; immediately qualified this as the suspect appearing to be in custody.
statements.notes: Uses both 'killer' and 'suspect' in same passage; qualification reduces certainty.

statements.claim: Said he, Blake Neff and Kirk were texting literally moments before Kirk went out to the crowd, discussing arguments Kirk could make.
statements.notes: Potentially verifiable from native messages.

statements.claim: Said a longtime crew member removed SD cards after the shooting to protect the footage and that the cards were in FBI possession.
statements.notes: Harpole later independently identified the AV worker and said footage was turned over.

statements.claim: Called theories that Frank Turek's hat gesture was a shooter signal baseless and defended Turek's character.
statements.notes: Opinion/character assessment, not direct evidence of shooter identity.

statements.claim: Relayed a surgeon's view that the projectile should have exited but did not, and asserted that the coroner found it just beneath the skin.
statements.status: Terminology discrepancy with later court record
statements.notes: Later court reporting describes a 'bullet fragment' recovered at autopsy.

statements.claim: Authenticated the circulated screenshot as a screen grab he had shared with others.
statements.notes: Direct admission.

statements.claim: Said he shared the private screenshot with a few people in government during the first roughly 33 hours so no lead would be ignored.
statements.notes: Creates a traceable evidence chain; identities/timestamps should exist in message records.

statements.claim: Explicitly said he was not an eyewitness and flew to Utah immediately afterward.
statements.notes: Important exclusion: do not attribute scene observations to Kolvet.

statements.claim: Said the leaked text was consistent with public frustrations, but described Kirk's overall Israel position as complicated, nuanced, and a months-long wrestle.
statements.status: Materially differs in framing from Neff
statements.notes: Neff immediately said there was no meaningful 'between'.

statements.claim: Said Kirk voiced the frustrations publicly and privately but tended to use a more moderate or tender tone in public.
statements.notes: Neff rejected this framing; Kolvet later said Kirk never said anything like the private message publicly on a show.

statements.claim: Said Kirk could not be controlled with money and was not bought and paid for.
statements.notes: Kirk could resist donor pressure while still being angered by threatened/withdrawn donations.

statements.claim: Explained he withheld the screenshot because it was private and said Kirk had not said anything like that private message publicly on a show.
statements.notes: Scope could mean exact wording/intensity rather than topic, but wording is materially narrower than AK010.

statements.claim: Said silence in public did not mean TPUSA was not asking questions or pursuing leads privately.
statements.notes: Private pursuit is difficult to independently audit without records.

statements.claim: Described Kirk as someone who spoke with unusually high directness and little equivocation in public.
statements.status: Tension with AK010 only if generalized
statements.notes: This was about Kirk's broad public style, not specifically Israel.

statements.claim: Said Kirk donated his salary and more back to Turning Point each year.
statements.notes: Not directly shooting-related; retained because it was an early post-shooting factual statement.

statements.claim: Publicly said continuing the campus tour was never in doubt because the team believed Kirk would have wanted it to continue.
statements.notes: No conflict.

statements.claim: Described being on campus on the day of the shooting and discussed his recent travel/work with Kirk.
statements.notes: Kolvet separately confirms Neff was there.

statements.claim: Confirmed the last-moment text discussion with Kirk concerned arguments for marriage/monogamy.
Said he had been advised not to comment on case details because as an eyewitness his public comments could affect a trial.
statements.notes: Explains limited public scene narrative.

statements.claim: Said the public and private material reflected the same underlying worldview rather than two different positions.
statements.notes: Neff explicitly rejected Kolvet's 'more moderate public tone' framing.

statements.claim: Said there was nothing hidden about Kirk's views on Israel.
statements.notes: Kolvet said the private message was not something Kirk said publicly on a show.

statements.claim: Described Kirk as wanting the Gaza war to end, opposing U.S. troops/refugee intake, caring about Israel, and becoming angry at pressure to deplatform allies.
statements.notes: Nuanced policy position is consistent with both pro-Israel support and criticism.

statements.claim: Said the people around Kirk did the best they could to help/save him and then followed Erika, Kolvet and Mikey McCoy in moving the organization forward.
Said chapter-start interest had surged from roughly 2,000 to tens of thousands after the killing.
statements.notes: Exact counts changed rapidly over time.

statements.role: Head of contracted personal-security detail / Integrity Security
statements.claim: Said his team had no ties to Israel, Mossad, or another foreign intelligence entity.
statements.status: No contrary evidence found in reviewed corpus
statements.notes: Negative claim limited to his team.

statements.claim: Said no Israel-specific or foreign-entity threat concern had been passed from Kirk or TPUSA security chief Dan Flood to his contracted team.
statements.status: NO CONFLICT with private Israel frustration
statements.notes: Policy/donor concerns are not the same as actionable security-threat intelligence.

statements.claim: Said the team routinely received threats against Kirk and assessed whether they were actionable.
statements.notes: General threat environment can coexist with no specific articulable threat for UVU.

statements.claim: Said UVU event information began coming to his team around Aug. 24 and planning/intelligence were kept in a timestamped operational system.
statements.notes: High-value records target.

statements.claim: Said his private team could not legally set up sniper/overwatch positions on campus rooftops and was responsible for close protection.
Described a pre-event message to UVU Chief Jeffrey Long about student access to Sorensen Center rooftop walkways and requested controlled access or a team member there.
statements.notes: Important nuance: the cited message concerned Sorensen access, not by name the Losee roof used by the shooter.

statements.claim: Said Long's final response to the access concern was that Harpole was covered, which Harpole understood as police taking responsibility for that area.
statements.notes: Should be checked against complete native thread and UVU records.

statements.claim: Said he increased his normal 8–9-person private detail to 12 plus a 13th driver because of the environment and expected crowd, despite no specific actionable threat.
Described expected crowd growth in roughly 1,500→2,000→3,000 terms.
statements.notes: Written UVU records released publicly only showed 200→600.

statements.claim: Said a security member was on Kirk within about two seconds and Harpole himself within about five seconds.
statements.notes: Relative estimates, not synchronized timestamps.

statements.claim: Said hospital clinicians obtained a pulse and took Kirk toward the operating room.
statements.status: Conflicts with literal 'died on scene' wording
statements.notes: Pulse restoration does not by itself establish neurologic viability.

statements.claim: Said an autopsy was performed and that he personally pushed for it to be done promptly.
statements.notes: KSL later reported the ME autopsy report was submitted in court.

statements.claim: Said he checked during transport and observed no exit wound.
statements.status: Generally consistent with later recovered projectile fragment
statements.notes: Not a substitute for ME findings.

statements.claim: Said he believed the visible wound was an entry wound based on what he saw while treating it.
statements.notes: He explicitly acknowledged he is not a doctor.

statements.claim: Identified the man handling the cameras/SD card as an AV contractor, not a member of his security detail.
Said the AV worker's footage was turned over to the FBI and that Harpole personally asked about it.
Said he saw no signs of an internal leak or betrayal within the security team that facilitated the attack.
statements.notes: Does not prove absence of a leak outside his visibility.

statements.claim: Said he still wanted answers about whether the accused shooter acted alone, had help, or was taking blame for others.
statements.notes: Harpole did not claim accomplices existed.

statements.claim: Said he was roughly 25–30 feet from Kirk when the single shot was fired.
Said he had expressed concern about surrounding buildings but Kirk appeared confident in his private security and local police.
statements.notes: Different speaker's concern; not evidence Kirk knew exact roof gap.

statements.claim: Said he joined the private SUV carrying Kirk about four miles to the hospital while the team attempted lifesaving measures.
Said Kirk was effectively gone immediately and did not suffer.
statements.notes: Uses clinical/spiritual language rather than formal legal time of death.

statements.claim: Also said doctors briefly restored a pulse at the hospital and a surgeon pronounced Kirk dead within roughly half an hour.
statements.status: Tension with literal reading of FT004
statements.notes: Strongly relevant to Erika's later 'died on scene' statement.

statements.claim: Said the team immediately contacted Erika Kirk, sent a plane to retrieve her, and called Vice President JD Vance.
Said he later found Kirk's cross necklace on/near his computer bag after the emergency transport.
Rejected the claim that touching his hat before the shooting was a signal to a gunman.
Thanked law enforcement for capturing the person she described as her husband's assassin.
statements.status: Consistent with arrest status; guilt not adjudicated
statements.notes: Robinson remains accused and has not entered a plea as of Aug. 2026.

statements.claim: In the same address referred to 'evildoers responsible' and used plural language about those who killed Kirk.
statements.status: Rhetorical ambiguity, NOT evidence of accomplices
statements.notes: Could refer to ideology/broader forces rather than multiple physical perpetrators.

statements.claim: Asserted that Kirk was killed because he preached patriotism, faith, and God's love.
statements.notes: Current court record still has disputed motive; defense contests prosecution's political-motive theory.

statements.claim: Also said she did not know what the event ultimately meant and that she believed God did.
statements.notes: Important context for EK003: rhetorical certainty on motive coexists with broader uncertainty.

statements.claim: Said Kirk's campus tour and movement would continue.
Said Mikey McCoy called her and told her Kirk had been shot and to get the children/security.
statements.notes: Corroborates McCoy's central role in immediate family notification.

statements.claim: Said the way the bullet struck Kirk caused him to die instantaneously and on the scene.
statements.status: MATERIAL CONFLICT with official hospital-death account + BH011/FT005
statements.notes: Likely describes irreversible fatal injury rather than formal time/place of death, but literal wording conflicts.

statements.claim: Said she had previously asked Kirk about wearing a protective vest and recalled him saying that if someone was going to get him, they would.
statements.status: No conflict with Harpole's no-specific-threat claim
statements.notes: Shows general personal safety concern, not necessarily actionable intelligence.

statements.claim: Said she insisted on seeing Kirk's body at the hospital after being advised not to.

statements.role: Senior Turning Point executive; described in sources as COO / former TPUSA COO
statements.claim: Said the staff had been leaning on one another and he was asking colleagues to write down memories of Kirk.
statements.notes: Not a shooting-evidence claim.

statements.claim: Said Kirk took little/no salary in early years and that Bowyer had personally approved payroll during part of that period.
statements.notes: Not directly case-related.

statements.claim: At the memorial, said his friend was murdered for using his voice to engage in peaceful dialogue.

Said chapter inquiries grew from roughly 60,000 around the memorial to about 130,000 by the interview.

statements.role: Kirk associate/mentor figure; not established here as TPUSA staff

conflicts.a_claim: Kirk voiced frustrations both publicly/private but softened public tone.
conflicts.b_claim: Public/private material reflected same worldview; Neff rejected 'moderate public tone' framing.
conflicts.reasoning: Two close colleagues explicitly characterize the same public/private gap differently.

conflicts.a_claim: Said Kirk stated these frustrations publicly and privately, with a softer public tone.
conflicts.b_claim: Later said Kirk never said anything like the private message publicly on a show.
conflicts.reasoning: Can be reconciled only by narrowing AK012 to exact wording/intensity; on its face the descriptions pull in different directions.

conflicts.a_claim: Said Kirk died instantaneously and on scene.
conflicts.b_claim: Official account says he was transported to a hospital and later died there.
conflicts.reasoning: Literal place/time-of-death wording conflicts with official contemporaneous account.

conflicts.a_claim: Said death was instantaneous/on scene.
conflicts.b_claim: Both described a pulse being obtained at the hospital before pronouncement.
conflicts.reasoning: A restored pulse is difficult to square with a literal claim of formal death on scene, though 'instantaneous' may mean irreversible injury.

conflicts.a_claim: Said Kirk was effectively gone immediately.
conflicts.b_claim: Also said a pulse was restored at hospital and death pronounced later.
conflicts.reasoning: Likely spiritual/irreversible-injury language rather than a claim about legal time of death.

conflicts.a_claim: Attributed killing to Kirk's patriotism, faith and message.
conflicts.b_claim: Prosecutors allege political motive; defense disputes motive and the case remains pretrial.
conflicts.reasoning: Her statement may be rhetorical, but it was not an evidentiary finding two days after the shooting.

conflicts.a_claim: Said Kirk was murdered for using his voice in peaceful dialogue.
conflicts.b_claim: Motive remains disputed in active litigation.
conflicts.reasoning: Memorial rhetoric should not be converted into proof of motive.

conflicts.a_claim: Referred to a singular assassin.
conflicts.b_claim: Also used plural 'evildoers' / 'they' language in same address.
conflicts.reasoning: Not a useful evidentiary contradiction; plural wording can refer to ideology/broader actors rather than multiple gunmen.

conflicts.a_claim: Kirk had strong donor/Israel-policy frustrations before death.
conflicts.b_claim: No Israel/foreign-entity threat warning was passed to contracted security.
conflicts.reasoning: Political/donor concerns are categorically different from actionable assassination-threat intelligence.

conflicts.a_claim: Team saw routine threats and rooftop access as security concerns.
conflicts.b_claim: Said staffing was increased despite no articulable/specific threat.
conflicts.reasoning: General vulnerability/routine hostile messages do not equal a specific credible threat to that event.

conflicts.a_claim: Understood Chief Long's reply as covering the roof-access concern.
conflicts.b_claim: The displayed message named Sorensen roof access; shooter roof was Losee.
conflicts.reasoning: Broad claims that police explicitly promised to secure the exact firing roof go beyond the text shown by Harpole.

conflicts.a_claim: Said later conversations revised expected crowd to 1,500–2,000.
conflicts.b_claim: Written planning documents showed 200 then 600.
conflicts.reasoning: Not necessarily contradictory if later verbal conversations occurred, but the larger estimate needs records/phone logs/messages for verification.

conflicts.a_claim: Said two UVU emergency medical personnel were on site.
conflicts.b_claim: Paperwork said EMS did not need to be scheduled and no first-aid station was needed.
conflicts.reasoning: Personnel may have been present without a formal scheduled EMS unit; not a logical contradiction by itself.

conflicts.a_claim: Said private team was increased to 12 plus a driver.
conflicts.b_claim: Said TPUSA security was increased to 12.
conflicts.reasoning: Substantively consistent.

conflicts.a_claim: Said crew member removed cards to preserve footage and cards went to FBI.
conflicts.b_claim: Said same person was an AV contractor and footage was turned over to FBI.
conflicts.reasoning: Two separate insiders give materially consistent account.

conflicts.a_claim: Said an autopsy was done.
conflicts.b_claim: Medical Examiner autopsy report was submitted at preliminary hearing.
conflicts.reasoning: Later court record strongly supports Harpole on this point.

conflicts.a_claim: Said projectile was found just beneath skin.
conflicts.b_claim: Later filings refer to a bullet fragment recovered at autopsy and inconclusive firearm comparison.
conflicts.reasoning: Could be the same damaged projectile described differently; not enough to call a contradiction without ME/ATF exhibits.

conflicts.a_claim: Said he was not an eyewitness.
conflicts.b_claim: Was an eyewitness; Kolvet separately said Neff was there.
conflicts.reasoning: Prevents accidental attribution of scene knowledge to Kolvet.

conflicts.a_claim: Search index shows a post saying Kirk's death was confirmed.
conflicts.b_speaker: Official death confirmation occurred later in afternoon, but exact Marx post time was not recovered.
conflicts.b_claim: Unverified timing claim
conflicts.confidence: Cannot establish that Marx knew before officials/family without the native post timestamp or archived capture.

conflicts.topic: General safety concern vs no specific threat
conflicts.a_claim: Said she had previously urged Kirk to consider a vest.
conflicts.b_claim: Said no specific actionable threat drove staffing increase.
conflicts.reasoning: A spouse's general fear is not the same thing as professional threat intelligence.

conflicts.a_claim: Said Kirk always had a succession plan and implied Erika.
conflicts.b_speaker: Erika took leadership and said movement/tour would continue.
conflicts.b_claim: Corroboration / continuity
conflicts.confidence: No contradiction identified in reviewed sources.

conflicts.a_claim: First referred to the 'killer' being in custody, then immediately said the suspect appeared to be in custody.
conflicts.b_claim: Robinson remains accused, not convicted.
conflicts.reasoning: Worth preserving because the first noun was overconfident, but Kolvet qualified it in the same breath.

ground_truth.fact: Utah DPS commissioner Beau Mason said Kirk was transported by private vehicle to a hospital and later died there.
ground_truth.notes: Official contemporaneous account; use for literal place-of-death comparison.

ground_truth.fact: Turek and Harpole separately said hospital clinicians briefly obtained a pulse before Kirk was pronounced dead.
ground_truth.notes: Multiple direct/near-direct accounts; not a formal medical record.

ground_truth.fact: KSL reported that a Utah Medical Examiner report following Kirk's autopsy was submitted during the preliminary hearing.
ground_truth.notes: Corroborates Harpole's statement that an autopsy occurred.

ground_truth.fact: Court-document reporting described a bullet fragment recovered during autopsy; ATF analysis did not conclusively connect it to the suspected rifle.
ground_truth.notes: Does not prove projectile came from a different gun; 'inconclusive' is not an exclusion.

ground_truth.fact: Released planning records documented an initial estimate around 200 and later 600.
ground_truth.notes: No released written record in that ABC set documented 1,500–2,000.

ground_truth.fact: UVU planning paperwork answered 'No' to scheduling EMS; committee notes said a first-aid station was not needed.
ground_truth.notes: Does not by itself prove no medically trained personnel were physically present.

ground_truth.fact: Harpole's displayed pre-event message specifically referred to student roof access at the Sorensen Center and requested controlled access or permission for his person to be there.
ground_truth.notes: Important limit when broader headlines say 'rooftops were covered.'

ground_truth.fact: Harpole's rooftop-warning message named Sorensen Center; the shooting was associated with the Losee Center roof in official/court accounts.
ground_truth.notes: This does not erase the general rooftop concern, but it prevents overclaiming that the text explicitly named the exact firing roof.

ground_truth.fact: Robinson remains charged, has not entered a plea, and final preliminary-hearing arguments are scheduled for Sept. 1, 2026; motive and some forensic interpretations remain disputed.
ground_truth.notes: Do not describe contested prosecution allegations as adjudicated facts.

methodology.implementation: Best-effort public corpus of case-relevant factual statements by Andrew Kolvet, Blake Neff, Brian Harpole, Frank Turek, Erika Kirk, Tyler Bowyer, Mikey McCoy, Victor Marx, and selected additional TPUSA figures/representatives. It is not literally every tribute, social reply, deleted post, private message, or paywalled/unindexed appearance.

No public search can prove completeness across deleted/private posts, unindexed video, ephemeral stories, radio appearances, or content blocked from retrieval. The Person_Summary sheet marks known gaps.
Statements are tight paraphrases rather than long verbatim quotations. Program timecodes and URLs are preserved so the original context can be checked.

Direct speaker disagreement; internal wording tension; material factual conflict; unresolved documentary discrepancy; unsupported/premature attribution; scope difference/no contradiction; corroboration.
Tyler Robinson is charged, has not entered a plea, and the preliminary-hearing process remains active as of Aug. 15, 2026. Prosecutor allegations are not treated as adjudicated facts.

Distinguishes irreversible/fatal injury, pulse restoration, clinical/legal pronouncement, and place of death. A witness saying someone was 'gone' is not automatically a statement of legal time of death.
Distinguishes general threats/vulnerabilities from a specific actionable or 'articulable' threat. This prevents false contradiction flags.

Harpole's displayed message concerned student roof access at Sorensen Center. Broad later shorthand about 'the rooftops' must not be silently converted into proof that the exact Losee firing roof was expressly named.
The strongest internal TPUSA disagreement is about whether Kirk's public statements materially softened what he said privately, not evidence that Israel was involved in the killing.

The public search index preserved the content of an early death-confirmation post but not a reliable exact posting time. Any claim that he announced the death before authorities/family requires native platform metadata or a timestamped archive.
Primary/direct transcripts and official/court records receive the most weight; later recollections are separated from synchronized timestamps; rhetoric and motive attributions are treated cautiously.
